issues.description: The problem statement's UML and task descriptions specify numberOfLecturers as an int, but the solution implementation declares the corresponding field as a byte and provides a setter taking a byte. This creates a structural mismatch: students reading the UML will expect an int attribute and corresponding int getter/setter signatures, while the solution uses byte for the attribute and setter parameter (the solution's getter returns int, which further highlights the inconsistency). This may confuse students about the correct attribute type and lead to mismatches when they implement getters/setters or when tests expect int signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of numberOfLecturers consistent across all artifacts. Preferably change the solution implementation to use int for the numberOfLecturers field and update the setter to accept int (and keep the getter returning int), so it matches the UML and task descriptions. Alternatively, if byte is intentional, update the problem statement/UML and any tests to specify byte for numberOfLecturers.
